dossier.public_summary: The 13.6-day dip disappears between sectors and its even and odd dips are 3.6 times different, with a p-value of 3.9e-9 for a constant depth. Two of the six dips alone carry most of the signal and are much deeper than the others. This is positive evidence for an eclipsing binary or blend on or near the target, not a 2.5 Earth-radius planet, as confirmed by a very low planet ranking of 0.06.

reasons.why: Odd and even dips differ at >6 sigma with depth_ratio 3.6, as expected for an eclipsing binary at twice the reported period (period_x2 27.2 d).
reasons.value: 6.413 (rapport_depth_odd 781.2 ppm per rapport_depth_even 2811 ppm, diff 2030 ppm, relation 3.6)

reasons.why: Individual transit depths are wildly inconsistent; signal is dominated by two deep outliers from two epochs, not a repeatable planet transit.
reasons.value: 1.5454192342407967e-20, share_of_top_3 0.982, outliers 3964 ppm (5.8 sigma) at BTJD 1738.951 and 3906 ppm (5.5 sigma) at BTJD 3584.648

reasons.why: Depth truly changes within the same TESS product (173 ppm in sector 57 vs 2747 ppm in sector 84) and χ² 42.07 dof 3, inconsistent with a fixed planet depth.
Independent scorer rates signal as highly non-planet-like, consistent with flat-bottom shape alone not being diagnostic for a diluted/blended binary.
